questions.question: What architecture separates software into independent services?
What software paradigm treats computation as mathematical functions?
What practice automates software delivery pipelines?
What software container platform packages applications?
What manages containerized applications at scale?
What technique optimizes code without changing behavior?
questions.explanation: Refactoring improves code structure and maintainability.

questions.question: What software design principle promotes loose coupling?
What license requires derivative works to be open source?
What pattern separates data from presentation?
What methodology develops software in short cycles?
questions.explanation: Scrum uses sprints for iterative development.

questions.question: Two developers edit the same lines of the same file on different branches; on merge, Git flags the overlap for manual resolution. What is this situation called?
questions.explanation: A merge conflict occurs when both branches change the same content and Git cannot auto-merge, requiring a human to choose or combine edits.

questions.question: A function always returns the same output for the same inputs and modifies nothing outside itself. Which functional-programming property does it have?
questions.explanation: Pure functions have no side effects and deterministic outputs, making them predictable, testable, and safe to run in parallel.

questions.question: An API call that charges a card must be safely retried after a timeout without charging twice. Which property makes repeating a request produce no extra effect?
questions.explanation: Idempotent operations yield the same result whether executed once or many times, so retries are safe.

questions.question: Which development methodology requires writing a failing automated test before writing the code that makes it pass?
questions.explanation: TDD follows the red-green-refactor cycle: write a failing test, write minimal code to pass it, then clean up.

questions.question: A library update breaks every caller because callers depended directly on its internal fields. Which design principle of hiding internals behind a stable interface was violated?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation exposes only a stable interface while keeping implementation details private, so internals can change safely.
